PR title:
Update regular expression for strip_ansi to handle edge cases

PR body:
#1216
Given this issue fixes an edge case in a regular expression, I wasn't sure how to add docs or testing.

Gold patch (use only to infer the symptom; do not quote or describe the fix):
diff --git a/CHANGES.rst b/CHANGES.rst
index ac1c51bf..217f705e 100644
--- a/CHANGES.rst
+++ b/CHANGES.rst
@@ -9,6 +9,8 @@ Unreleased
 -   Fix link in ``unicode_literals`` error message. :pr:`1151`
 -   Add support for colored output on UNIX Jupyter notebooks.
     :issue:`1185`
+-   Operations that strip ANSI controls will strip the cursor hide/show
+    sequences. :issue:`1216`
 -   Remove unused compat shim for ``bytes``. :pr:`1195`
 -   Expand testing around termui, especially getchar on Windows.
     :issue:`1116`
diff --git a/click/_compat.py b/click/_compat.py
index cf6e1c99..4709b88e 100644
--- a/click/_compat.py
+++ b/click/_compat.py
@@ -16,7 +16,7 @@ WIN = sys.platform.startswith('win') and not APP_ENGINE and not MSYS2
 DEFAULT_COLUMNS = 80
 
 
-_ansi_re = re.compile(r'\033\[((?:\d|;)*)([a-zA-Z])')
+_ansi_re = re.compile(r"\033\[[;?0-9]*[a-zA-Z]")
 
 
 def get_filesystem_encoding():

message.content: Operations that strip ANSI control sequences from text do not remove cursor hide/show sequences.
